q: what contributed to Creamy Cropmen's success this week against Shake and Blake and what hurt Shake and Blake? What decisions were made that really helped or hurt either, if any other than luck of players playing well or poorly
short: Cropmen lead 978 to 603 with three days left. Blake left about 184 points on the bench this week (73 Monday, 111 Tuesday) and got only 26 on Thursday against Cropmen's 163, while Cropmen kept a near optimal lineup.
answer:
This matchup is not finished. It is Friday and three days (Fri, Sat, Sun) remain, but Creamy Cropmen lead 978 to 603 (a 375 point gap). Before the week started, Shake and Blake were projected 1625.7 to 1402.4, so Blake was the favorite by about 223. That is a 600 point swing, and most of it came from three things.

1. Lineup decisions hurt Shake and Blake (about 184 points left on the bench). Monday: started 305 against an optimal 378. VJ Edgecombe (47) and Josh Hart (37) sat on the bench while Andrew Nembhard (0), Toumani Camara (11) and Kris Dunn (23) started. Tuesday was worse: 272 against an optimal 383, a loss of 111. Naz Reid (48), Derrick Jones Jr. (39) and Tari Eason (27) were on the bench, and Jayson Tatum and Josh Hart started and scored 0. Some of that may be late scratches or injuries I can't confirm from this data, but the bench points were real. Blake's lineup loss this season is 205 points, 184 of them this week. Cropmen lost only 17 this week.

2. Schedule and Thursday. Thursday's slate was the biggest single gap: Cropmen scored 163 (Franz Wagner 61, Wendell Carter Jr. 64, Davion Mitchell 38) and Blake scored 26 (only Pelle Larsson). The preseason projection already had Thursday at 92 for Cropmen and 6.5 for Blake, so this was a built-in edge for Cropmen.

3. Cropmen's pickups and depth. Cropmen are the most active team in the league (18 adds, 13 drops) and kept their lineup nearly optimal (417 of 422 on Monday, 398 of 410 on Tuesday). Luka Doncic gave them 87 and 63. Streamers helped: Derik Queen (added Wed, 39), Saddiq Bey (40) and Davion Mitchell (53 on Tuesday). Not every pickup worked: Jaylen Wells scored 6. Haliburton and Kawhi are on IR and Cropmen's injury cost is only 98 points this week. Today they added P.J. Washington and Devin Vassell, which is not yet in the scores.

What Blake did right: the one move this week was adding Tari Eason (27 on Tuesday) for Camara, but Eason sat on the bench that day, so it didn't help. Blake's injuries are small (only Josh Hart, about 5 points), so injuries are not the story. This was a lineup management problem plus a schedule problem.

Going forward: Blake's remaining three days project to 765 and Cropmen's to 774.5, so a comeback is very unlikely. I did not search the web, since this is a question about data already in the league files.
